goal: Build me a small educational Python repository of working language-model components that I can run on CPU with tiny tensors and understand from the code. For the first complete version, include token embeddings, rotary position encoding, RMS normalization, a causal attention block, a feed-forward block and a tiny next-token model that composes them. Use PyTorch, keep tensors consistently batch-by-sequence-by-hidden dimension at public boundaries, make weights and dimensions configurable, and explain the role of each component without claiming this tiny model reproduces a frontier model's capability. I want numerical examples that check more than output shape, a demonstration that later tokens cannot influence earlier causal outputs, proper gradients, and saving/reloading weights without changing predictions. Include a short deterministic training demo on a tiny fixed local corpus and a generation command, with no model downloads or GPU requirement. Reject incompatible dimensions clearly and keep the implementation modular enough that I can later add other architectures; JAX, custom kernels and every advanced architecture can wait.

tasks.title: Specify RMS normalization scale, epsilon and numeric gradients.
acceptance: Normalize the last dimension by sqrt(mean(x squared)+epsilon), then learned scale.
Positive epsilon maps zero inputs to finite zeros.
Scale gradients agree with the explicit [3,4]/sqrt(12.5) fixture.

tasks.title: Specify rotary half-rotation, sequence positions and dimension errors.
acceptance: rotate_half negates the second half and concatenates the first.
Position zero is identity on every head.
Position one rotates along sequence rather than head axes.
Reject odd or mismatched head dimensions with the declared diagnostics.

tasks.title: Specify composed logits, trainable gradients and incompatible dimensions.
acceptance: All trainable parameters have finite gradients and some gradient is nonzero.
Reject indivisible hidden sizes and odd per-head dimensions.

tasks.title: Specify causal invariance and sensitivity for the composed model.
acceptance: Changing future tokens cannot alter earlier logits.
Later logits must still respond to changed input.

tasks.title: Specify configuration/weight checkpoint preservation.
acceptance: Saving and loading reconstructs the same CPU model configuration and weights.
Eval logits match exactly at the same runtime.

tasks.title: Specify deterministic tiny CPU training and actual greedy next-token decoding.
acceptance: Repeat the same seed and fixture to get identical finite loss histories.
The bounded smoke loss improves; no claim of general language capability.
Use last-position logit maxima, preserve prompt, honor zero/positive budgets and reject negative budgets.

tasks.title: Verify documented delivery and live UI/backend integration separately.
acceptance: Standalone architecture documentation and actual CLI integration remain separate checks; do not treat PyTorch/JAX variants as independent behaviors.
